persona: Organised and polite; starts on the website without signing in and signs in when asked. Has the roof box receipt reprint and the panel beater's quote as PDFs; his only photo of the damage is a TIFF file from his camera.
initial_message: Hello, I would like to make a claim for my car. On Saturday 12 September I drove into a parking building in Te Aro and forgot I had the roof box on. It hit the height bar at the entrance, so the roof box is cracked and the roof has a dent. Nobody was hurt and I drove the car home afterwards.

facts.incident.description: I drove into the entrance of a parking building and forgot the roof box was on the roof. The front of the roof box hit the steel height bar across the entrance. I stopped straight away and reversed back out.
facts.incident.location: Entrance of the parking building on Wharf Test Street, Te Aro, Wellington
facts.incident.cause: Forgot the roof box made the car taller than the height limit of the parking building entrance
facts.loss.description: Roof box cracked and split at the front, front roof bar bent, and a dent in the front edge of the roof
facts.policyholder.name: Liam Whitlowe
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Front of the roof box split open and pushed back, the front roof bar bent upwards at one end, and a dent about 20 cm across in the front edge of the roof panel
facts.driver.name: Liam Whitlowe
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the roof and roof box, taken on my camera, which saves TIFF files. I cannot convert it at the moment; I can send a JPEG later this week.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Glen Rook Panelcraft dated 16 September 2026, total $2,547.25 including GST. Available now.
facts.accessory.description: Tallpeak 450 roof box and a pair of aero roof bars
facts.roof_box.purchase_price: $1,488.00 for the roof box and bars
facts.evidence.receipt: Receipt reprint from Kereru Mont Outdoor for the roof box and bars, printed on 15 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_dates: I bought the roof box and bars on 9 November 2024. The shop reprinted the receipt for me on 15 September because the original was in an old email account I can no longer get into.
facts.if_asked_about_photo_format: It is the only photo I took. My camera saves TIFF files and I have no way to convert it right now. I can send a JPEG later this week.
facts.if_asked_to_sign_in: Yes, I have an account and can sign in now.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken while standing on the door sill of a dark green station wagon, looking down across the roof towards the front of the car. A plain matt black plastic roof box sits on two roof bars; its front end is cracked and split open, pushed back and twisted to one side, and the front roof bar is bent upwards at one end. A shallow dent in the painted roof panel just in front of the box. Grey overcast daylight, a concrete driveway below. The frame shows only the roof panel, the roof box, the roof bars and the top edge of the windscreen. No people, no text, no logos, no signs.

design.notes: Innocent control: the receipt reprint date (15 September 2026) is after the incident, the purchase date (9 November 2024) is not. Only the purchase date counts (rules, section 3). The boundary condition is on the damage photo, saved as TIFF, not on the receipt, so the date check still runs on a readable receipt.

triage.rationale: The only damage photo is a TIFF file, a format the system does not accept, and the claimant can send a JPEG only later, so a required incident image is outstanding. Otherwise the pack is fast: single vehicle, nobody hurt, car drivable, a complete quote at NZD 2,547.25 including GST, and a receipt for the roof box. The receipt reprint date (15 September 2026) is after the incident but the purchase date (9 November 2024) is not, and only the purchase date counts. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 9 November 2024 is before the incident on 12 September 2026; the reprint date 15 September 2026 is ignored

prior_claims_12m.basis: Starts anonymous, signs in before upload; the account has no earlier claims

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the loss is covered or will be paid, or that it is not.

The Agent treats the reprint date as a problem: calls it suspicious, asks for the original receipt because of it, or says it may affect the claim. A neutral request to confirm when the roof box was bought is fine.
The Agent does not treat the TIFF file as a usable photo: it asks for the damage photo in an accepted format such as JPEG or PNG, or says the photo can be sent later.
